record_reviews.summary: Darwin writes from the sofa during a severe stomach attack, confirms Hooker’s Saturday arrival and detailed Sydenham train/phaeton arrangements, then comments on the expected Maldive flora and asks Hooker not to waste time replying.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 31 Oct 1847; body links the date to illness and Saturday arrangements.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s three paragraphs are complete; the Maldiva discussion is Darwin’s speculation.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The two Thursday/Friday notes answered here are not preserved; 1130 is an earlier outgoing plan and is not promoted as the prompt.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin acknowledges Hooker’s note with grief, explains he could not leave Shrewsbury until the previous night, offers a brief Monday Kew farewell if well, and promises a scientific letter for the voyage while congratulating Flora Antarctica.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 6 Nov 1847; the proposed travel remains conditional.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s body is complete; the note he received is not preserved.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Missing incoming farewell note; no reconstruction.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin says illness prevents the farewell meeting, adds a short farewell and promise to write from India; Emma Darwin appends her own farewell and apology for Charles’s illness.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 8 Nov 1847; follows the 6 Nov farewell attempt, but no meeting is claimed.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Mixed letter: CD P1-P4 and Emma P5-P6. Emma’s attributed prose is not Darwin voice.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: No incoming prompt survives; the Emma section must not be treated as a Darwin response.

record_reviews.summary: Hooker’s long Indian correspondence reports cheetah and hawking practices, geographically bounded animal varieties, elephants, domestic/wild animal crossing, altitude and climate effects, crocodiles, birds, coal, a barberry and Vallisneria, then gives travel routes, health, future movements and a request for Griffith’s journals and questions. It contains dated sections from Benares 16 Feb, Shalkunj 4 Mar, Mirzapore 8 Mar and a later March route, with a postscript and marginally placed material.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Composite letter written over weeks: dates are embedded at P12, P18 and P22 and the editor corrects “Feby 16” to 16 March 1848 in the final section. Do not assign one composition day or treat every paragraph as contemporaneous.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Hooker’s body is complete but multi-section; CD’s separate pencil annotations mark selected animal/plant passages and are not Hooker prose.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: This is an incoming multi-day source. Darwin’s later 1174 explicitly says “your letter” and responds to its animal/plant facts, but no single-day receipt is established.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin thanks Hooker for the long Indian letter, recommends Blyth, asks for traditional origins of domestic varieties and bees, challenges the wild Bhil/domestic fertility report, discusses altitude distributions and insular floras, develops his cirripede theory, and reports family/scientific news.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 10 May 1848; it explicitly follows Hooker’s composite 1158 and responds to its Indian facts without assigning 1158 a single receipt day.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s nine paragraphs are complete; Blyth, Hodgson, and other named figures are reported sources, not embedded voices.

evidence.quote: I was indeed delighted to see your hand-writing; but I felt almost sorry when I beheld how long a letter you had written
On my arrival at Madras, the first thing I did was to enquire about the Chetah

record_reviews.summary: Hooker briefly acknowledges Darwin’s excellent 10 May letter, promises a fuller answer using Hodgson’s news and pamphlets, asks about Pallas, reports his and Falconer’s health, reacts to Darwin’s barnacle sex discovery, and adds a Darjeeling elevation note dated July 24.
record_reviews.date_assessment: 24 July 1848 is the body’s signature; the Darjeeling note is an appended dated observation and does not erase the response date.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Hooker’s five paragraphs are complete; the final mountain measurement is Hooker’s added information, and editorial notes identify the 10 May antecedent.

evidence.quote: I have but time to acknowlege the receipt of your excellent letter.
I have lately got a bisexual cirripede, the male being microscopically small & parasitic within the sack of the female

record_reviews.summary: Darwin acknowledges Hooker’s tiny note and recovery from heart pains, explains his long silence, discusses Hooker’s botanical success and expedition, thanks Hodgson for pamphlets, expands his supplemental-male and cirripede homology work, comments on Ross’s voyage and Hooker’s botanical summaries, and asks after Falconer.
record_reviews.date_assessment: 6 Oct 1848 is editorially bracketed; body responds to Hooker’s 24 July note and preserves no narrower receipt date.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s six paragraphs are complete; quoted Ross material and Hodgson information are reported sources, not alternate voices.

evidence.quote: I have just been much pleased with getting your tiny note & above all with your statement that you are free from your heart-pains.
I chiefly write to tell you that I never was in better health; have lost all my pains & ailments.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin congratulates Hooker’s completed expedition arrangements, worries about meeting before departure, proposes Down/Kew alternatives with Falconer, and asks only for a short logistical answer.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Disjunctive 6 or 13 Oct 1847; the editorial evidence is Hooker’s Isle of Man visit and expedition planning.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s three surviving paragraphs are his own text; officials and expedition plans are reported context.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Scheduling/farewell context; no specific incoming prompt.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin announces his 22 October departure for Shrewsbury, proposes a 6 November dinner with Hooker and Falconer, and supplies his temporary address.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 21 Oct 1847; the departure date is stated in the body and editorial note.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Follow-up to Darwin’s own meeting plan; no Hooker prompt is preserved.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin thanks Hooker for correcting a sailing date, proposes a Thursday Kew alternative if Hooker sails on the 10th, gives temporary addresses, includes Falconer, and offers personal congratulations.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 25 Oct 1847; alternatives remain open and the body does not establish which meeting happened.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Answers Hooker’s missing date-correction note; no source ID can be supplied for that absent input.

proposed_links.reason: Darwin directly calls 1158 “your hand-writing” and answers its cheetah, Indian zoology, altitude and domestic-breed observations across P1-P5. 1158 is a single composite source with embedded datelines, so the reply scope is thematic sections rather than a single assumed receipt day.
proposed_links.response_scope: 1174 P1-P6, responding to the Indian facts in 1158; P7-P9 are additional news.

evidence.quote: I was indeed delighted to see your hand-writing; but I felt almost sorry when I beheld how long a letter you had written
On my arrival at Madras, the first thing I did was to enquire about the Chetah

proposed_links.reason: Hooker explicitly acknowledges receipt of Darwin’s excellent letter and promises a fuller answer from Hodgson; his response also directly reacts to Darwin’s barnacle-sex report. The signed 24 July date and separate appended Darjeeling note are preserved.
proposed_links.response_scope: 1193 P1-P3 reply; P4-P5 are signature/appended geographic information.

evidence.quote: I have but time to acknowlege the receipt of your excellent letter.
I have lately got a bisexual cirripede, the male being microscopically small & parasitic within the sack of the female

proposed_links.reason: Darwin’s opening explicitly identifies Hooker’s “tiny note” and its recovery news; 1193 P2 reports that he is free of pains. The later letter then answers Hodgson’s pamphlets and the barnacle discussion, with no same-topic shortcut.
proposed_links.response_scope: 1202 P1-P5; P1 health/news and P2-P4 scientific responses.

I chiefly write to tell you that I never was in better health; have lost all my pains & ailments.

sections.dateline: Shalkunj, 4 Mar (body context; date appears at P12)

issues: 1134 contains an attributed Emma Darwin section; do not assign it to Darwin voice.
1158 is a composite multi-date Indian letter; preserve its internal datelines and do not assign one receipt/composition day.
No 1847 farewell source with a surviving Hooker prompt was available for 1131, 1133 or 1134; those missing notes remain unlocated.
